hero.title: Four SketchUp plugins for the daily work of landscape professionals
hero.subtitle: Take-off, site surveys, materials, selection: tools that absorb the repetitive steps of a landscape project in SketchUp.

value.title: What these plugins take care of

items.title: From drawing to quote
items.text: Measuring happens straight on the model, and the quantities land in a spreadsheet you can build your quote from.

items.title: From survey to model
items.text: A surveyor's coordinate file becomes a usable set of 3D points, with nothing to retype.

items.title: Fewer repetitive steps
items.text: Searching for materials, sorting them into folders, selecting by criteria: everyday handling that costs less time on heavy models.

products.title: The four plugins
products.intro: Each one answers a specific task in the day-to-day of a landscape project.

compatibility.intro: Every plugin is developed and tested against recent releases of the host application.

status.title: Where {siteName} stands
status.body: The four plugins are written and working. They are not on sale yet: a trial with a small group of professionals is planned before anything is released. If this is relevant to your work, leave your address and you will hear about it.

cta.title: Get notified at launch
cta.body: An email address is all it takes. It will only be used to announce that the plugins are available.

quantisketch.summary: Click the elements in your drawing to add them to a basket — areas, lengths, objects — then export the basket to Excel to build the quote.
quantisketch.metaDescription: Click elements in the model to build a basket of quantities — areas, lengths, objects — then export it to Excel as the basis for your quote.

features.title: A basket of quantities
features.text: Every element you click in the drawing joins the basket, which you can review as the take-off goes along.

features.title: Areas, lengths and objects
features.text: The three kinds of quantity a landscape project needs sit in the same basket.

features.title: Export to Excel
features.text: The basket leaves as a spreadsheet, ready to serve as the basis for the quote.

steps.title: Open the basket
steps.text: It stays within reach while you work on the model.

steps.title: Click the elements to measure
steps.text: Each click adds the element and its quantity to the basket.

steps.title: Export to Excel
steps.text: The resulting file mirrors the contents of the basket.

csvPoints.summary: A surveyor's CSV file becomes a set of 3D points inside SketchUp, carrying their labels and their layers.
csvPoints.metaTitle: {name} — from surveyor's file to SketchUp model
csvPoints.metaDescription: Turn a CSV coordinate file into 3D points inside SketchUp, with labels and layers, without retyping anything.

features.title: Reads the coordinate file
features.text: The CSV your surveyor sends is read as it is, with no prior conversion.

features.title: 3D points in the model
features.text: Each coordinate row becomes a point placed in the model.

features.title: Labels carried over
features.text: Points keep the label from the survey, so you can tell them apart in the model.

features.title: Spread across layers
features.text: Points are assigned to layers, so you can show or hide them by group.

steps.title: Get the survey CSV
steps.text: The coordinate file exactly as your surveyor's tool produces it.

steps.title: Run the import
steps.text: The plugin reads the file and creates the points in the model.

steps.title: Work on the survey
steps.text: The points are in place, with their labels and their layers.

paletteXl.summary: A roomier way to handle materials and components than the built-in panel: a larger window, search by name, and folders of your own.
paletteXl.metaDescription: A larger window for SketchUp materials and components, with search by name and folders you organise yourself.

features.title: A larger window
features.text: More room on screen to browse through materials and components.

features.title: Search by name
features.text: Find an item by typing its name instead of scrolling the list.

features.title: Folders of your own
features.text: Items are filed into folders, following whatever order suits you.

features.title: Materials and components together
features.text: Both kinds of item are handled from the same window.

steps.title: Open the window
steps.text: It stands in for the built-in panel while you work.

steps.title: Search or browse
steps.text: By name, or by walking through your folders.

steps.title: Apply to the model
steps.text: The item you pick is applied the usual way.

multiSelect.summary: Select several entities of the model at once by criteria, instead of one by one — which starts to matter once a project grows large.
multiSelect.metaDescription: Select many entities of a SketchUp model at once by criteria, rather than one by one, on large projects.

features.title: Selection by criteria
features.text: Matching entities are picked up from the criteria you set, with no click on each one.

features.title: Several entities at once
features.text: The resulting selection behaves like any other SketchUp selection.

features.title: Built for heavy models
features.text: The gain grows with the size of the project, where selecting by hand becomes expensive.

steps.title: Set the criteria
steps.text: They decide which entities are picked up.

steps.title: Work on the whole set
steps.text: From there it behaves like a selection made by hand.

about.title: About
about.intro: {siteName} is the work of an independent developer, who writes and maintains the four plugins alone.

sections.title: Who builds this
sections.body: There is no team behind these plugins: design, Ruby development and keeping up with SketchUp releases are all handled by one person. Which means you talk to that person directly, with nobody in between.

sections.title: The approach
sections.body: Each plugin starts from one precise, repetitive task in SketchUp, and stops there. Nothing is added for the sake of a longer feature list: a tool that does one thing well is easier to learn and easier to fix.

sections.title: Where the project stands
sections.body: The four plugins work and are tested on {app} {versions} under {os}. Behaviour on Mac has not been tested to date. Nothing is on sale yet: a trial with a small group of professionals is planned, and their feedback will shape what comes next.

sections.body: The contact form collects your email address and, if you choose to fill them in, your name and your message. Nothing else is asked for. No account is created and no payment is handled on this site.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You have the right to access, correct, erase, restrict and object to the processing of your data, as well as the right to data portability. To exercise them: [[TO COMPLETE: how to exercise these rights, dedicated address and response time]]. You may also lodge a complaint with the French data protection authority (CNIL).

sections.title: Protection against abuse
sections.body: To limit automated submissions, the number of messages sent from one connection is capped. This measure does not keep your IP address: only a non-reversible fingerprint is stored for one hour, then erased.
